These resources support the course; They don't replace him. Add to Appendix C of Volume 2 (manuals) A1, grammars, Anki, Forvo, Aswaat Arabiyya, Al Jazeera Learning Arabic, italki), which remain valid. Each tab indicates recipients, level, advantages, limits, cost and way of use. The new information was checked on the pages indicated as the source on 19 October 2026. Prices, editions and availability change: check them again before buying. When a data was not indicated in a reliable source, the card says so. How to choose. In A2 There are three main tools: a dictionary ordered by root, a collection of verbal tables and a source of authentic slow listening. The dialect material is added only after the decision of A2-24.
C1 · Dictionaries by root
A Dictionary of Modern Written Arabic (Arabic) · "Hans Wehr" by J Milton Cowan · Spoken Language Services, 4ISBN 9780879500030.
• Targets: Who reads English and wants the Arabic-English dictionary of reference for modern Arabic written.
• Level: A2 onward; becomes indispensable by B1.

• Advantages: entries are alphabetically sorted by root; under each root the derived forms are indicated with Roman numerals (II, III, IV...), as in Grammar G36; about 1300 pages in the pocket edition.
• Limits: in English; for the most recent words of the media can be dated; does not cover dialects.
• Cost: variable according to the dealer (a retailer indicated USD 25,00, with uncertain availability).
• Use during the course: from A2-01, for root-based research; when a word is not in the vocabulary, seek the root and then form.
• Sources: card at Mecca Books · user guide •How to use the Hans

The Arabic Dictionary · Eros Baldissera (Zanichelli) See Volume 2, Appendix C4. It is the Arabic-Italian bilingual dictionary recommended from A2: use it to verify plurality and meanings in English; for the root order and richness of derived forms, alongside Hans Wehr.
C2 · Verbs and grammar
Arabic Verbs & Essentials of Grammar Jane Wightwick, Mahmoud Gaafar · McGraw Hill, 3edition, © 2018 · ISBN 9781260030990 (paper), 9781260031003 (eBook).
• Recipients: who wants a quick consultation of the verbs and basic grammar.
• Level: A2 (The publisher presents it for beginners and for those looking for a quick reference).
• Advantages: verbal tables for regular verbs, weak, doubled and with hamza; For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions shall apply:
conjunctive, juxtaposed, imperative, maṣdar; index of 400 frequent verbs linked to the tables; twelve short audio lessons on the root system via the publisher app.
• Limits: in English; summary explanations; the number of pages is not indicated on the publisher's page.
• Cost: USD 27,00 paper; USD 24,00 eBook (US publisher's prices).
• Use during the course: to control a conjugation while writing, next to the G tabs21–G36.
• Source: mheducation.com
Grammar of modern standard Arabic · Mion, D'Anna (Hoepli) View Volume 2, Appendix C2. In A2 becomes the main reference in English for verbal morphology and syntax of complex phrases (G32–G38).
C3 · Manual in English

Communicate in Arabic · Levels A2-B1 of the Common European Framework for Languages Monica Ruocco, Daniela Potenza, Souzan Fatayer, Mohammed Hussein Eid · Hoepli, series Oriental Studies, April 2023 · ISBN 9788820399139 (paper), 9788836013449 (digital).
• Recipients: Italophones who have completed a journey A1 of standard Arabic.
• Level: A2-B1; second volume of a course in three volumes (A1-A2, A2-B1, B1-B2).

• Benefits: 12 Theme units built on dialogues and texts of increasing difficulty, with grammar, squares of Vocabulary and various exercises; one review every four units; Arab-Italian and Italian-Arab thematic glossary; cultural notes and dialects; MP audio3 downloadable; XIV-258 pages.
• Limits: also covers the B1, then in A2 the first half is used; digital content requires the platform of the publisher.
• Cost: € 32,90 paper; € 26,99 Digital (Publisher's Price).
• Use during the course: second source of exercises and listening, especially in the module A2.4 (practical situations); use it after the corresponding unit of this volume, not in place of it.
• Source: hoeplieditore.it
C4 · Authentic listening and reading

Aswaat Arabiyya and Al Jazeera Learning Arabic 2, Appendix C6). In A2: A2-19, a high Novice level track or low intermediate of Aswaat Arabiyya per week, with activities before, during and after listening; from A2-23, a weekly news of the lowest levels of the section       .News in Levels of Al Jazeera Learning Arabic, with the strategy in three listenings. Some passages of Aswaat Arabiyya contain dialect: in A2 serve as an exercise in recognition (A2-23), not as a model.
C5 · Egyptian: after dialect choice
Kallimni ʿArabi Bishweesh · A Beginners' Course in Spoken Egyptian Arabic 1 Samia Louis · The American University in Cairo Press, 2011 · ISBN 9789774162206.
• Targets: who starts systematic study of the spoken Egyptian Arabic.

• Level: Egyptian beginner; first volume of a series that continues with an intermediate volume (Kalimni) ʿArabi ISBN 9789774249778, aimed at those who have about 40 hours of standard Arabic; or 30 of dialect) and with advanced volumes.

• Advantages: functional approach according to ACTFL guidelines; ten modules of two lessons each on daily situations (health, telephone and numbers, purchases, directions, habits, invitations, services, restaurant); glossary; online audio recorded by Egyptian speakers.
• Limits: in English; the editor's page doesn't say if the texts use Arabic writing, transliteration or both: check it before buying.
• Cost: GBP 29,99 · USD 35,00 · EGP 700 (Publisher's prices).
• Use during the course: starting book of the EGY track in B1, if A2-24 Choose the Egyptian. In A2 it does not need:
enough A2-23 and the EGY deck.
Source: aucpress.com
C6 · External certification
CIMA · Certificat international de maîtrise en arabe Institut du monde arabe (IMA), Paris. Updating the Volume tab 2.
• Targets: those who want an external and independent feedback of their standard Arabic level.
• Level: six levels CEFR, from A1 a C2.

• Tests: oral understanding (44 multiple choice questions, 60 minutes); written understanding (44 questions to multiple choice, 60 minutes); written production (three tasks in 60 minutes: the first of 40–60 words, others of 50–100); individual oral production (three tasks at most, 11 minutes, recorded). In all less than three hours.

• Advantages: more than fifty approved centres in almost twenty countries, including Italy; valid certificate 3 years; age minimum 15 years; can be repeated, with at least 60 days between two sessions.
• Limits: the reading test texts are not vocized, as in printing; dates and locations depend on Centers.
• Cost: determined by the examination centre; the candidate's guide does not indicate any amounts.

• Use during the course: the end ofA2 is the first time recommended (Plan, section 6.4). Prepare with Readings without module vowels A2.4 and with simulation of A2-24; points out that the examination A2 of this course does not equal CIMA.
Source: CIMA candidate's guide (version) 5.2, updated to 15 June 2023, published on imarabe.org)
C7 · Voice synthesis for scripts

As in Volume 2, the catalogue does not indicate a specific app. For scripts in fuṣḥā uses an Arabic voice (not an Italian voice reading Arabic) and compares the result with the tutor. For Egyptian scripts of A2-23 vocal synthesis is not suitable: an Egyptian speaker is needed.
